title: Securing an IP-Blocking Playbook
context: You must automate the response to scans coming from an external IP. The playbook will run hundreds of times per day: three decisions will determine its reliability.

n1.text: An alert reports an external IP scanning multiple servers. What is the first step of the playbook?

choices.text: Qualify the alert and enrich context (reputation, history, targeted assets)
choices.why: Automation must act only after qualification: otherwise it amplifies false positives.

choices.text: Immediately block the entire address without verification
choices.why: Without qualification, the playbook may block a legitimate partner.

choices.text: Classify the alert as a false positive by default
choices.why: That turns automation into a false-negative generator.

n2.text: The risk score exceeds the threshold. How do you design the blocking action?

choices.text: Guardrails: scope limited to the IP, bounded duration, logging, ticket, and planned reversibility
choices.why: Guardrails prevent a qualification error from spreading across the entire network.

choices.text: Block a /0 to be sure to cover the attacker
choices.why: That would cut off all traffic: the action is disproportionate and practically irreversible.

choices.text: Execute the block without logging to save time
choices.why: Without logs, it is impossible to audit, understand, or roll back the action.

n3.text: The playbook is deployed. How do you ensure continuous improvement?

choices.text: Measure effects, monitor false positives, and adjust logic with rollback capability
choices.why: Continuous improvement and reversibility are at the heart of automation considerations.

choices.text: Never modify the playbook again to guarantee stability
choices.why: An unadjusted playbook becomes ineffective when context changes.
Without measurement, you cannot detect playbook drift.

n4.outcome: Your playbook qualifies before acting, bounds its impact with guardrails, and improves through measurement.

debrief: Automation logic must be understood and documented before any deployment.
Guardrails, logging, and reversibility are mandatory for production actions.
Continuous improvement comes from measuring false positives and tuning rules.
